questions.q: Define situational irony and give one example from "जूठन" where the outcome is the opposite of what the characters or reader expect.
questions.a: Situational irony occurs when events turn out opposite to what is anticipated. In "जूठन", the headmaster, who should uphold education and equality, forces the Dalit protagonist to clean the school premises — a task that reinforces caste hierarchy instead of dismantling it. A wrong answer (e.g., "the boy is sad") shows the student confuses irony with mere misfortune or emotional tone, missing the structural contradiction between role and action.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the name "जूठन" functions as a symbol. What abstract idea does it represent beyond its literal meaning of "leftover food"?
questions.a: The name "जूठन" symbolizes the Dalit community's treatment as social leftovers — discarded, considered impure, and denied dignity. It represents systemic dehumanization where an entire group is reduced to waste. A wrong answer (e.g., "it's just a nickname") reveals the student reads the name literally and misses the symbolic compression of caste oppression into a single word.

questions.q: Identify an instance of dramatic irony in the story where the reader knows more than a character. Describe the scene and explain the effect on the reader.
questions.a: When the headmaster praises the school's "discipline" and "cleanliness" (p. 71) while the reader knows this cleanliness is maintained by forcing a child to sweep instead of study, dramatic irony arises. The reader sees the hypocrisy the headmaster ignores. A wrong answer (e.g., "the boy feels bad") indicates the student cannot distinguish dramatic irony from character emotion; they must recognize the knowledge gap between reader and character.

questions.q: Compare the broom (बुहारना) and the school building as symbols. How does each symbol reveal a different dimension of caste oppression?
questions.a: The broom symbolizes forced menial labor imposed on Dalit children — the physical enactment of caste duty. The school building symbolizes the institution that legitimizes this oppression under the guise of education. Together, they show oppression as both daily practice (broom) and structural sanction (building). A wrong answer treating both as "just objects" fails to analyze how symbols operate at different levels: one micro (daily act), one macro (institutional framework).

questions.q: Evaluate the author's use of verbal irony in the dialogue between the headmaster and the protagonist's father (pp. 72-73). Does it strengthen or weaken the critique of casteism? Justify.
questions.a: The headmaster's polite, "reasonable" tone while denying the boy's right to education — e.g., "नियम हैं" (rules exist) — is verbal irony: his words claim fairness but enact exclusion. This strengthens the critique by exposing how casteism hides behind bureaucratic language. A wrong answer (e.g., "the headmaster is polite") misses the ironic gap between speech and intent, showing the student cannot detect tone-based irony.

questions.q: Create a new symbolic object that could appear in a modern sequel to "जूठन" to represent the persistence of caste discrimination in urban schools. Explain its significance in 2-3 sentences.
questions.a: A cracked digital tablet given only to Dalit students while others receive new ones — symbolizing the "digital divide" as the new broom. It represents how technological access replaces sweeping as the marker of exclusion. A poor answer (e.g., "a broken chair") lacks connection to contemporary structural inequality, showing the student cannot transfer symbolic thinking to new contexts.
